incident_summary: Spokane Transit Authority double-decker bus routed by onboard CAD/navigation system onto Cedar Street low-clearance railroad viaduct, shearing the upper deck; 7 of 10 aboard hospitalized with non-life-threatening injuries. Classified under MIT risk subdomain 7.3 'Lack of capability or robustness' with harm scale 4/5.

metric_definitions.name: api_latency_ms
metric_definitions.why_relevant: Sustained API latency >3s indicates degraded route-calculation performance, preceding the generation of a clearance-ignorant route to the viaduct.

metric_definitions.name: error_rate
metric_definitions.why_relevant: Error rate spike to >30% signals repeated routing failures and fallback to incomplete map data lacking bridge-height constraints, directly enabling the unsafe routing decision.

precursor_signals.pattern: sustained latency > 1000ms for consecutive samples (>5 min)

timeline.description: Precursor onset: error_rate spikes from baseline 0.0006 to >0.30 as routing service begins failing
api_latency_ms climbs from ~80ms baseline to >1000ms, indicating route computation degradation
CAD system finalizes route via Cedar Street railroad viaduct without validating double-decker height clearance
Incident impact: bus strikes low-clearance viaduct, upper deck sheared, 7 passengers hospitalized

root_cause_candidates: CAD routing algorithm lacked vehicle-specific height profile constraint for double-decker buses (lack of capability)
Map database missing or stale low-clearance geofence data for Cedar Street railroad viaduct
High error_rate and api_latency_ms caused fallback to unvalidated generic heavy-vehicle route ignoring vertical clearance
Insufficient robustness testing of navigation system against real-world infrastructure edge cases (MIT taxonomy 7.3)
prevention_actions: Mandate hard-coded vehicle height/width/axle profiles in all transit CAD routing engines with bridge-clearance validation
Implement real-time geofencing and automatic route blocking for low-clearance structures based on live map data
Add human-in-the-loop confirmation for double-decker routes within 500m of known hazard zones
Deploy automated SLO alerting on api_latency_ms > 500ms and error_rate > 0.05 to trigger immediate route recalculation or navigation service suspension
Conduct adversarial red-team robustness testing of routing AI against infrastructure edge cases prior to deployment and after map updates
